text:
claire: FYI found partner payload landed in our ingest bucket that contains a base64 KMS ciphertext and a header `kms_key: projects/partner-prod/locations/global/keyRings/k1/cryptoKeys/partner-wrap`. The object key is `partner-a/2026-02-13/wrap-sa.json.b64`.

omar: Do we know if that was expected? Our onboarding doc says partners must either use our KMS or provide signed attestations.

claire: Not expected. The metadata has `x-origin: partner-ci` but no onboarding ticket. I pulled the object to quarantine: moved to `s3://sec-quarantine/INC-2026-2077/` and set object-lock.

sec-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-2077 (severity: medium)  tags: secrets,kms,s3,onboarding.

maria: Thanks. Immediate triage checklist: 1) confirm whether we decrypted it anywhere, 2) check Vault for entries referencing that object or fields like `wrapped_credential`, 3) block further uploads from that partner origin, 4) notify partner contact and request pause.

devops: Quick log scan: no Vault decrypts or transit/rewrap calls in the last 7 days for that ciphertext. However, there are three Vault entries under `secret/data/partners/partner-a/*` that contain `wrapped_blob` keys that match the object size. I'm exporting paths now.

omar: Good find. Next: RBAC scope on KMS. If the partner-owned key was allowed to encrypt/decrypt into our project via a grant, we need to narrow it. Who has iam: Service Account that could have been granted?

maria: I'll check Cloud IAM history. Also we should add an ingestion-layer validation to reject uploads where `kms_key` is not in our allowlist. That will be low cost and prevent recurrence.

claire: For immediate mitigation I added a temporary WAF rule to reject POSTs containing `wrapped_credential` and blocked the partner IP range at the edge.

sec-bot: Added task: run KMS audit export for `Encrypt`/`Decrypt` / `AsymmetricSign` calls for the last 30d -> deliver to INC ticket.

devops: Ran a quick query: there are zero Decrypt calls from our project tied to that partner key. So they are uploading wrapped artifacts but we haven't been decrypting them. That reduces blast radius.

omar: Still, we have stored wrapped blobs. We should rotate our own transit keys for any secrets we control that were created from those blobs, and mark partner blobs as untrusted until they provide an approved workflow. Proposed sequence: 1) snapshot current secrets list, 2) rotate transit key `partners-rotational`, 3) rewrap partner blobs that we control into `partners-rotational` and replace stored values, 4) add metadata `origin=partner-unverified`.

maria: Agreed. Also add a mandatory pre-accept step to the partner onboarding checklist: partners must provide either (A) our KMS key id to encrypt with, (B) a signed manifest with key thumbprint and rotation schedule, or (C) use a secure transfer channel to provide plaintext which we then rewrap. I'll create a PR to update onboarding docs.

claire: Who will contact partner? I can start comms but need the account owner included.

omar: I will take partner comms. Ask them to stop uploads immediately and provide proof of key ownership, rotation schedule, and the purpose of the uploaded blob. If they don't respond in 4 hours escalate to account team.

devops: I'll prepare the rewrap runbook and a dry-run in staging. Steps will include: do not log plaintext, perform rewrap via `vault write transit/rewrap ciphertext=<old> key=partners-rotational`, then test consumer services. Schedule 200 secrets per maintenance window to limit risk.

maria: RBAC actions: remove any project-level broad grants that allow third-party principals to use our KMS keys. Limit `roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter` to explicit service accounts and add conditions to timebox grants. Also ensure KMS admin and data-access audit logs are exported to SIEM.

sec-bot: Incident INC-2026-2077 updated by maria  status: investigating  postmortem:required.

claire: Action owners and ETA: quarantine done (claire), search for other artifacts (devops, 30m), rewrap runbook draft (devops, 2h), partner comms (omar, now), onboarding PR (maria, 24h), ingestion validation PR (engineering, 48h).

omar: Noted. Also recommend a small detection rule: alert when an S3 object metadata `kms_key` does not match allowlist. I can prototype a lambda to validate on PUT.

maria: Good. We'll include that in the remediation and add it to the postmortem action list.

claire: Thanks team — keeping ticket updated.
